Let

\[
I=\iint_D\left(x\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}+y\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\right)\,dx\,dy,
\qquad D=\{(x,y):x^2+y^2\le 1\}.
\]

Use polar coordinates \((r,\theta)\). Since

\[
x\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}+y\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}
= r\frac{\partial f}{\partial r},
\]

we have

\[
I=\int_0^1\int_0^{2\pi} r\frac{\partial f}{\partial r}\,r\,d\theta\,dr
=\int_0^1 r\left(\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{\partial f}{\partial r}\,r\,d\theta\right)dr.
\]

But on the circle \(x^2+y^2=r^2\),

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial r}=\frac{\partial f}{\partial n},
\]

so

\[
\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{\partial f}{\partial r}\,r\,d\theta
=
\int_{\partial B_r}\frac{\partial f}{\partial n}\,ds,
\]

where \(B_r=\{(x,y):x^2+y^2\le r^2\}\). By the divergence theorem,

\[
\int_{\partial B_r}\frac{\partial f}{\partial n}\,ds
=
\iint_{B_r}\Delta f\,dx\,dy.
\]

Given \(\Delta f=e^{-(x^2+y^2)}\), we get

\[
\iint_{B_r}e^{-(x^2+y^2)}\,dx\,dy
=
\int_0^r\int_0^{2\pi} e^{-s^2}s\,d\theta\,ds
=
2\pi\int_0^r s e^{-s^2}\,ds.
\]

Now

\[
\int_0^r s e^{-s^2}\,ds
=
\frac12\left(1-e^{-r^2}\right),
\]

so

\[
\int_{\partial B_r}\frac{\partial f}{\partial n}\,ds
=
\pi\left(1-e^{-r^2}\right).
\]

Therefore,

\[
I=\int_0^1 r\pi\left(1-e^{-r^2}\right)\,dr.
\]

Compute the integral:

\[
I=\pi\left(\int_0^1 r\,dr-\int_0^1 r e^{-r^2}\,dr\right).
\]

We have

\[
\int_0^1 r\,dr=\frac12,
\]

and with \(u=r^2\),

\[
\int_0^1 r e^{-r^2}\,dr
=
\frac12\int_0^1 e^{-u}\,du
=
\frac12\left(1-e^{-1}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
I=\pi\left(\frac12-\frac12(1-e^{-1})\right)
=\frac{\pi}{2e}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{\pi}{2e}}
\]
